extracted.intended_audience: journalists, media researchers, policymakers, and media industry stakeholders interested in the Australian news ecosystem
extracted.subtask_description: A country-level profile of the Australian news ecosystem summarising audience behaviours, industry structure, regulation, funding, trust, misinformation, and technology impacts. Designed to inform researchers, policymakers and industry participants about the state of news in Australia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Population
rubrics_metrics.description: Population: 26 million
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic contextual demographic metric used to scale audience and market figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet penetration
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet penetration: 90%
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicator of digital access and potential online news reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local news availability / news deserts
rubrics_metrics.description: Australia now has 29 local government areas with no local news publishers, TV, or radio servicing the local community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures geographic gaps in local news provision; used to identify communities underserved by local media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Print media financial pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: Print media have been hit hard due to the decline in advertising revenue and rising print costs. Government departments are cutting back print advertising and instead rolling out campaigns on social media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains structural causes of print decline and how changes in government ad purchasing affect local/regional outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government advertising spend on regional news
rubrics_metrics.description: Currently the local, state, and federal governments spend about 1% of their advertising budget on regional news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantifies public-sector support for regional news and signals policy leverage to support regional outlets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streaming services weekly reach vs free-to-air TV
rubrics_metrics.description: Streaming services weekly reach (58%) has surpassed that of free-to-air TV (54%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience reach comparison showing shift from broadcast TV to streaming platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscriber churn/reductions due to cost-of-living
rubrics_metrics.description: One in three subscribers say they have reduced their subscriptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures the financial pressure on paid digital news and streaming subscriptions driven by broader economic conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streaming local content spend and proposed quotas
rubrics_metrics.description: Major streaming services reduced their spending on local content by 11% (A$46m). Government promised to introduce a quota system for streaming services in 2024; industry advocates a 20% local content quota while streaming platforms lobby for 2%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines data on local-content investment with the regulatory debate over quota levels; useful for evaluating cultural-policy impacts on local production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform commercial engagement with news (Meta/Google) and regulatory response
rubrics_metrics.description: Meta pulled back from news in Australia, closing its Australian news partnerships team and not entering new commercial deals. Current deals reported worth A$70m annually. Under the News Media Bargaining Code, Google and Meta are together paying news publishers roughly A$200m a year on voluntary content agreements; many agreements expire this year. Calls exist to 'designate' Meta under the Code, which would force negotiation or face fines of 10% of annual Australian revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes platform behaviour, monetary flows to publishers, regulatory mechanisms (News Media Bargaining Code), and policy options (designation and fines) that affect publisher-platform relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital advertising concentration
rubrics_metrics.description: Google and Meta’s combined advertising revenue in Australia was A$8.3bn in 2023, more than half of all digital ad revenues (A$14.2bn).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantifies market concentration in digital ad markets and its significance for news industry revenue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted public funding for media diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: A$10.5m in funding through the News Media Assistance Program to promote a diverse and sustainable media sector; the ACMA has received funding to implement the Media Diversity Measurement Framework.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details government support programs and measurement frameworks intended to assess and promote media diversity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public broadcaster strategy and obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: ABC continued its transition into a digital-first media organisation; ABC Five-Year Plan forecasts that by 2028 most audience engagement will come through digital services. Chair priorities include securing better funding for the ABC and upholding its Charter responsibilities, including the requirement for impartiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames the role and strategic orientation of the public broadcaster and the importance of funding and charter obligations (e.g., impartiality) for public-service journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevalence and effects of misinformation (case study: Voice referendum)
rubrics_metrics.description: Misinformation was abundant during the Voice referendum campaign; widespread false claims (e.g., would lead to tax increases, AEC tampering) revealed deep distrust in government. Seven in ten Australians expressed concern about lies and misinformation on social media during the campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses a high-profile referendum as an example of misinformation dynamics and public concern; indicates impacts on democratic discourse and demand for quality news.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI adoption in newsrooms and public attitudes
rubrics_metrics.description: AI increasingly permeates newsrooms (News Corp Australia producing 3,000 articles a week using AI). Public concern: over half (57%) believe AI creates more problems than it solves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures both industry uptake of generative/automated tools and public sentiment, suggesting need for policy frameworks to balance benefits and public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust in news – headline metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Trust in news overall: 40%. Trust dropped this year by 3 percentage points, reaching its lowest point since 2020. The drop was largest among women.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-level metric of public confidence in news used to assess media legitimacy and audience relationships over time and across demographics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Top trust factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Top trust factors were 'high journalistic standards' (81%) and 'transparency' (80%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies which attributes of news organisations most strongly correlate with public trust; useful for editorial and governance priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most trusted news sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Public broadcasters such as ABC and SBS are the most trusted sources of news surveyed, along with regional and local newspapers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Source-level trust ranking that informs where audiences place confidence and which outlets might best serve public-information needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press freedom ranking and score (RSF World Press Freedom Index)
rubrics_metrics.description: RSF World Press Freedom Index: 39/180; Score 73.42.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: International comparative indicator of press freedom based on expert assessment; useful for cross-country benchmarking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay-for-online-news penetration
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay for online news: 21%
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proportion of the population paying for online news subscriptions; indicates commercial viability of paid models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Podcast reach
rubrics_metrics.description: Listen to podcast in the last month: 40%
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience behaviour metric showing uptake of audio formats and opportunities for publishers.
